title: November flow gave no clear added March forecast gain beyond prior March and time at three Arctic gauges in 29 winters
abstract: We tested whether November flow improves March forecasts after prior March flow and time are known. We used ArcticGRO v20261104 at Ob, Lena and Yenisey, with earlier-year fits and 29 common approved winters in 1981-2011. Adding November flow reduced equal-river mean squared log-flow error by 13.78%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was -2.33% to 25.06%. The main test gives no clear added gain. Last-25-winter fits gave 19.17% (9.62% to 26.63%). Without time, the gain was 23.46% (9.02% to 31.78%). Thus, the evidence depends on the training period and model. November plus time alone did not clearly beat prior March plus time. Few gauges, revised data, regulation, gaps and conditional intervals limit inference. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and arithmetic checks support reproduction. External source and record-level tables remain outside the package.

display.caption: November flow gave an uncertain main gain after prior March and time. Shorter-training and no-time checks gave clearer gains. Intervals condition on the fitted predictions.
